dialogue_text: We are most faithfulto what we never dared to claim.
Is something wrong?
It is nothing, Your Grace.
Are you going to call me "Your Grace" again?
Are you going to call me "Your Grace" again? I wasn't aware the title had become optional.
I wasn't aware the title had become optional. Last night, you called me Kael.
Kael...
Judgement tends to blur at night. And now? Inconveniently clear, Your Grace.
Inconveniently clear, Your Grace. In three days, my betrothal will be announced.
To whom?
Her Majesty. She needs my army. I need the authority of the Crown.
I need the authority of the Crown. Then I suppose congratulations are in order... I understand. I knew you would.
For someone who spends every day confined to the piano, you seem surprisingly at ease in the snow. The winter air is rather refreshing, Your Grace.
The winter air is rather refreshing, Your Grace. The piece you played last winter. Play it at the announcement. The Nocturne? Yes.
It is rather dark for a celebration. If you smile while you play, the nobility would dance to a funeral march.
How fortunate that their ears are so accommodating. Can you do it?
If that is what Your Grace desires. As always.
Three days later.
His Grace keeps his pet pianist close. A fallen house cannot survive on music alone.
A fallen house cannot survive on music alone. How discerning your ears are, gentlemen.
How discerning your ears are, gentlemen. Music escapes you, yet gossip never does. Lord Julius, we were merely— Of course. Merely bored. But boredom need not be relieved at another man's expense.
I didn't ask for help. Nor did I offer it. I cannot abide an instrument out of tune.
Julius. I know. A relief. My parents spent a fortune on the name.
Nocturne? You recognize it?
Enough to wish I'd heard the rest. You infer a great deal from a single performance. I did not infer. I listened.
Shouldn't you be with the others? Should I? They seem rather eager to have you.
They seem rather eager to have you. They usually are. And yet you're here. Since last winter. Worth the wait.
Ian. Your Grace.
Behold, Her Majesty the Empress.
Then tell me to stop.
Then tell me to stop. I don't want you to.
The betrothal of Her Imperial Majesty the Empress and His Grace the Grand Duke is hereby proclaimed.
the Grand Duke is hereby proclaimed.
His Grace selected tonight's performance, I believe. I did. Then let us hear it. As you wish, Your Majesty.
As you wish, Your Majesty.
You stopped. No one was listening.
I was.
You owe me nothing for my patronage, Ian. Nothing beyond your music. And even that remains yours.
NOCTURNE
Mr. Ian. His Grace has returned.
Your Grace, what... What... what are you doing? Your Grace, please stop.
Your Grace, please stop. Forgive me.
Go away, Ian.
Go away, Ian. This is... my choice.
Then tell me to stop.
Then tell me to stop. I don't want you to.
I cannot promise you a future, Ian. I've been to war before.
I've been to war before. I've lost men to orders I couldn't change. I was responsible for them, but some decisions were never mine to make.
but some decisions were never mine to make. I won't put myself or this house in that position again. If that means I have to marry for power someday...
If that means I have to marry for power someday... I will. I understand, Your Grace.
I understand, Your Grace.
Magnificent, Ian. Simply magnificent. Thank you.
Thank you. If you'll excuse me.
If you'll excuse me.
It sounded different tonight.
It sounded different tonight. That obvious? Only if one had heard it before. Last winter, it sounded as though you were waiting for someone.
it sounded as though you were waiting for someone. Tonight, it sounded like goodbye. Perhaps I needed it too. Then I won't ask to whom.
Then I won't ask to whom. Unusually considerate. I have my moments.
You brought music to a betrothed? One should never arrive unarmed. -This is yours. -Unfortunately.
-Unfortunately. It isn't terrible. From you, I shall take that as applause. Third bar.
I knew you'd find it. You stop before the phrase resolves. I couldn't decide where it should go.
Then don't decide yet. All right. I find myself in need of professional supervision. And I happen to have a piano that deserves rescuing.
And I happen to have a piano that deserves rescuing. Would you visit me on Thursday? To rescue the piano? Solely in the interest of the instrument.
Your pianist left his music behind.
Your pianist left his music behind. Have it sent to my carriage. Your carriage? He returns with my household. Of course.
Of course. Tuned every month, played almost never.
That's cruel. To the piano? Obviously. I see where I rank.
You're staring. I'm listening. With your eyes. Family failing.
Family failing. Third bar. Play it. Absolutely not.
Absolutely not. Sit down. You played it wrong.
Very. You kept going. Stopping would have made it worse.
Come back. We should finish it. The piece?
The piece? I was hoping you'd assume so. Is that you?
Is that you? Unfortunately. You look very serious. I was 6. You were trying very hard.
It's rather charming. The portrait? The portrait. Of course.
You left this.
You left this. I didn't even notice. May I?
You could've sent someone. I could have.
Better. Thank you, Lord Julius. Good night, Ian.
Good night. Come in.
Come in. Two nights ago, you left before the final toast.
I had finished playing. The evening was not over. For me, it was. You were in the garden. For air. With Lord Julius.
With Lord Julius. And conversation. He seems to provide both. You were at his house today. I was invited to play.
There are pianos here. I know. Look at me.
Forgive me, Your Grace.
Forgive me, Your Grace.
You were crying.
Yes, Your Grace. Why?
I thought I could bear it better than I did.
I thought I could bear it better than I did. I thought we understood each other.
So did I.
I didn't want you to leave last night.
I didn't want you to leave last night. I know.
I never wanted this to take anything from us.
For you, perhaps.
Ian.
Excuse me, Your Grace.
Mister Ian's recital, Your Grace. The smaller hall is nearly full. Reserve the larger hall.
Reserve the larger hall. Yes, Your Grace.
The third bar again, if you would. Again? Unless you prefer it wrong. I was hoping you'd call it distinctive. I considered it.
I considered it. And? Wrong was more accurate. You've been reading the same line for some time. Perhaps I'm being thorough. Is it improving?
Is it improving? No. Then we may blame the composer.
I'm afraid I'm rather poor company today. I hadn't realized I was meant to be entertained. You needn't be. Come, tea asks less of a man than music.
Come, tea asks less of a man than music. I'm rehearsing at Western Hall on Tuesday. Am I being informed or invited?
Am I being informed or invited? Take it as you like. Tuesday, then.
You're early.
You're early. I wanted to see wether you make mistakes when no one is watching. And? I remain hopeful.
And?
And? I wasn't sure you wanted applause. You usually aren't so cautious. I'm trying something new. It wasn't meant for applause. Alright.
Alright. Is there something I might do for you?
Why? You haven't seemed quite yourself of late. Have I been so obvious? Not especially.
Not especially. I simply make a habit of noticing things. You are so strange. So I've been told. Which seat is mine?
Which seat is mine? Third row on the right, near the aisle. Good. Good?
You'll know where I am.
Your Grace.
Your Grace. Please.
May I? Come in.
I brought you something. Flowers? Before the performance? Only a few.
Anything larger would require an announcement. You shouldn't have. I know.
Then why did you? I wanted to. Thank you.
30 minutes, Mister Ian. I should let you prepare. You can stay! Alright.
Say something. About what? Anything.
That painting is dreadful. That's what you chose? You said anything.
You're impossible. I can discuss the curtains? Please don't. Sensible.
Your Grace. The northern pass is snowbound.
The northern pass is snowbound. Colonel Voss wants to force the supply convoy through tonight, with two companies as escort.
Better a day than two companies.
It's me. Come in. What happened?
I dropped the water. You were magnificent.
You were magnificent. You came. Did you think I wouldn't?
You are trembling.
I'm cold.
Is it warm now? Yes.
Yes. Your Grace.
Lord Julius? Yes.
Your Grace.
Lord Julius. You came. I was invited.
So I gathered. He'll be tired.
He'll be tired. I expect he knows.
Shall we?
Not yet. Not yet? Yeah. I told Julius I would see him after.
I told Julius I would see him after. I can wait.
You needn't. Ian.
I'll return later. Ian.
May I hold you?
May I hold you?
Yes. Your Grace.
You found me.
I told you I'd see you after.
You changed.
I spilled water. Difficult recital? The recital was fine.
I'm not quite ready to say goodnight.
A little longer, then.
Your left hand in the tea room. Something's wrong, isn't it?
Something's wrong, isn't it? It's nothing. Does His Grace know?
Does His Grace know? He noticed. And?
I told him it was nothing. Do you think it's nothing?
I thought it would pass.
You should see a physician. I know. Will you?
Will you? I haven't decided. I could arrange it. You don't know me well enough to ask that.
You don't know me well enough to ask that.
Good night, Ian. Good night.
Are you at ease with me?
Why do you ask? I've been assuming you were.
I want to be.
I need you to take command.
I need you to take command. How soon? Within a fortnight. How many men?
The latest figures are in the dispatch. Provisions are being assembled. Then we prepare for the earlier date.
Is it about Mr Arden? Ian said he thought he could bear it better than he did.
Ian said he thought he could bear it better than he did. Most people would find it difficult to be loved only in the shadows.
He knew it would happen. Knowing is not quite the same as living through it.
Your Majesty. Mr Arden, I heard Western Hall was a great success.
Mr Arden, I heard Western Hall was a great success. You are very kind, Your Majesty. Not kindness. I have reliable ears. I should like you to play at next month's recital
I should like you to play at next month's recital at the Imperial Hall, if you would accept the invitation.
It would be an honour, Your Majesty. Then I shall look forward to it.
I keep picturing you at the Imperial Hall.
Do you? They'll be fortunate to hear you. You've heard me often enough. Not nearly.
Not nearly.
Are you at ease with me? Why do you ask?
I've been assuming you were. I want to be.
Will you stay, Your Grace? Yes.
At most, 14 days. Winter provisions are counted twice.
Winter provisions are counted twice. Rotate the horses before the first regiment moves.
And I want every field surgeon supplied before anyone leaves this estate. We will not spend men to save time.
Yes, Your Grace.
Mister Arden has arrived, sir.
Mister Arden has arrived, sir.
I wasn't certain you'd come back. Neither was I. I was unkind. A little.
You might have pretended otherwise. I considered it. You were right.
You were right. That's unfortunate.
It's been getting worse. Sometimes it's only a moment.
Sometimes I cannot make it do what I ask. Her Majesty asked me to play at the Imperial Hall next month.
I should have been pleased.
I was terrified. If I cannot play,
I don't know what remains of me.
Then let me find out.
I know it cannot be easy for you.
But you should tell His Grace. Whatever lies between you, this is another matter.
this is another matter. I know.
Do try the cake. It's rather good.
Have you tried it?
Have you tried it? Three pieces, just to be certain. And are you? Perhaps one more.
Come around here. Thank you.
Ian, I'm...
Ian, I'm... Don't. You don't need to apologize.
May I talk to you? Of course. Sit here.
It's my left hand.
It's been getting worse. How long has this been happening?
For a while. I thought it would pass.
Sometimes it won't do what I ask. I didn't know how to tell you. That morning,
That morning, you said it was nothing. You should have told me.
You've been dealing with this alone.
May I? Have you seen anyone about it?
Have you seen anyone about it? No, Your Grace. I'd like someone to examine it. Would you let me arrange that?
Yes. It'll be all right.
Which fingers?
Which fingers? These two. They go numb. I suspect pressure on a nerve here, at theelbow.
Can it be treated? It may improve. I cannot yet say how much.
I have a recital next month. No practicing for now. We shall examine you again before it.
I see. Your Grace, please see that Mr Arden getsenough rest.
Your Grace, please see that Mr Arden getsenough rest. Of course. We leave for the north within a fortnight.
So soon? Perhaps sooner. How long? I wish I could tell you.
I wish I could tell you. Your Grace. Will you be home for dinner? Yes.
Then I shall see you there.
Have you found anything? A book I already own. A successful morning, then.
A successful morning, then. For the bookseller. You saw the physician? A nerve, apparently. No practicing.
A nerve, apparently. No practicing. For how long? He declined to be precise. Then you'll have to listen to all mymistakes.
Your second movement especially. Should I be concerned? Probably.
Bring it next time. You're meant to be resting. You can play. Then I'd better practice.
Then I'd better practice. You're always so kind to me. You make it rather easy.
You make it rather easy. About the other day…
You don't have to tell me how you feel. Not now. Thank you.
I should be going. Of course, Julius.
Must you go? You're occupied. Not now.
You're not following. Not the music.
You were saying?
You were saying? I'm afraid I've lost my place.
Where is that going? The west wing of the palace, sir.
They're taking the piano to the palace. I should have asked you.
I'm sorry. I'll have them stop. Were you going to tell me? Yes. I had rooms prepared near the garden.
Yes. I had rooms prepared near the garden. You've already decided, then, Your Grace.
I wanted you with me. As your pianist? As yourself.
As yourself. And what would they call me there? You would remain part of my household.
You would remain part of my household. That wasn't what I meant.
I should like to stay here with you. I know.
Would you come back here? Whenever I could. And when you couldn't? I would be at the palace.
With Her Majesty. Yes. I cannot put my men at the mercy of thecourt.
I haven't forgotten. And after the wedding?
And after the wedding? Would you still want me here? More than I ought.
I have been happy here.
That is why I keep staying.
But I don't know what to call us.
I'm hurting you, Ian. And I still don't know how to want you less.
Ian.
Ian. Wait.
Your Grace.
I must ask you to end my patronage. Ian. Please.
Please take it.
Give me a moment.
Are you leaving me? I have to. Must it be tonight?
I have been putting it off.
You were never only my pianist. No. But it was the only thing we were that had a name.
But it was the only thing we were that had a name. I never held that over you. I know. You didn't have to.
You gave me a home. You gave me somewhere to play.
They meant everything. That's why it took me so long to leave. I'm so sorry for hurting you like this.
I'm so sorry for hurting you like this.
I love you. I know. I wanted you to choose me.
I wanted you to choose me. I'm choosing you now. As what?
I can't ask you to put me before your country.
Before your house. I wanted your love to be enough.
I wanted your love to be enough.
I can't ask you to stay... but I don't know how to let you go.
I was fool to think being together would make this bearable for you.
Ian... Please... I'm so sorry.
This doesn't change what I said. I know.
Stay tonight. Only tonight.
You should sleep.
You first.
If you'd like, I can have it sent to your new home.
If you'd like, I can have it sent to your new home. May I think about it? Of course.
You left this after the announcement.
Keep it. It's yours. I wrote it for you.
It was the closest to I ever came to asking.
I asked you to play at the announcement. Yes.
Ian...
You've been practising. A little.
More than a little. I was hoping you'd noticed.
And the Imperial Hall? Have you heard anything?
Her Majesty has written. The invitation will remain open until I'm ready to play again.
The invitation will remain open until I'm ready to play again. That's good news. It is.
It is. She's been very generous. I've been working on something.
I've been working on something. May I see it? When there's rather more of it.
It's the second movement. I should look forward to it.
I should look forward to it.
From Her Majesty, Your Grace. As you requested, Mr Arden's invitation to the Imperial Hall will remain open until he is ready to perform.
As you requested, Mr Arden's invitation to the Imperial Hall will remain open until he is ready to perform.
The northern road is clear. Supplies will arrive tomorrow. Thank you.
Thank you. You play the piano, I believe. Would you look at this?
It's a beautiful piece.
Whenever I came home from the front, I'd fall asleep listening to him play this. I thought it peaceful.
I thought it peaceful. To me, Your Grace, there's a deep longing in it.
Your Grace, the eastern outpost is under attack.
Very well. I'm coming.
We are most faithful to what we never dared to claim. To be continued... (And there is a post-credit scene.)
Your Highness?
